card holders

BHATTACHARJEE:

AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:

to increase the prices of foodgrains for BPL
and APL categories;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

Government are going to cut down the

Curbing the rising prices of pulses
and other food items
*82. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the prices of pulses and other food items
including vegetables have risen abnormally
which are beyond the reach of lower middle
class people;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
specific reasons for the increase despite
bumper crop of wheat and sugarcane in the
country during the current year; and

to curb the price rise and the result thereof?
Relief package for suicide
prone areas
*83. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: W ill the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether any relief package has been
announced for the suicide prone areas in
the country for the benefit of farmers;
and
(b) if so, the districts likely to be covered
under that package?

*84. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
breast cancer cases are alarmingly increasing
in the country since last three years;
(b) if so, Government’s views and
reactions thereto;
(c) whether Government have any
proposal for making available breast cancer
screening test at free of cost to ordinary
people of our country;
(d) if so, by when it will be
implemented; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Shifting of Guwahati railway station
*85. SHRIMATI  SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Railway
authorities are considering a proposal for
shifting of the Guwahati Railway Station
from its present site and a proposal has
also been mooted to enlarge the Kamakhya
station and shift the railway line from its

completed?
Salem Railway Division
*86. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to

(a) whether it is a fact that the Railways
had decided to bring in the areas now with
the Palakkad Division under Salem Railway
Division;

has been allotted for the purpose of Salem
Division; and

Road railway station
*87. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a proposal has been made
by the Finance Minister of Orissa to
develop the Jajpur-Keonjhar Road railway
station taking into account Kalinga Nagar
an industrial hub in the making;

(c) what is the action plan of
Government to revamp the above station
to cater to the needs of passengers and
transporters in view of fast
industrialization of this area?
Permission for duty free import of
wheat
†*88. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have given
permission to private sector for duty free
import of wheat from companies of USA;

28
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

imported wheat per quintal;
(c) whether Government have given
permission to restrict the excess quantity
of weeds and insecticides and to relax
quality standard in the imported wheat;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
‘Beeja Yatra’ by social activists
*89. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
‘Beeja Yatra’ being undertaken by eminent
social activists, to liberate Indian agriculture
from the grip of foreign companies;
(b) the steps being taken to meet the
demands raised in the Yatra; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Committee on working of AIIMS
*90. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRI LALIT SURI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether after great discontentment
and indiscipline in the working of AIIMS,
Government have set up a three-member
Committee to look into the functioning of
AIIMS and prescribe a remedy;
(b) if so, by what time the panel has
been asked to submit its report alongwith
the details of members and terms of
reference of Committee;
(c) whether AIIMS is loosing its
credibility as the quality and functioning
of AIIMS over the past three to four years
has not been satisfactory;
(d) if so, what other steps are being consi-
dered to restore its normal functioning; and
(e) whether the recent confrontation
between the Minister and the Director has
further worsened the position?
Electronic waste
†*91. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether environmentalists have
expressed concern over the damage to the
environment due to increasing electronic
waste;
(b) whether Government have sought
suggestions from environmentalists for
resolving this problem;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) whether Government are considering
to enact a law to prevent the damage to the
environment by E-waste?
Fixing MSP of cotton
*92. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Minimum Support
Price (MSP) of cotton, is fixed in such a
manner that the farmers are unable to get
back even the production cost of their crops
and are compelled to commit suicide due to
debt;
(b) if so, the justification thereof;
(c) the number of farmers’
representatives and their percentage against
the total number of members in the
Committee which fixes the MSP;

29
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(d) the steps taken by Government for
taking farmers into confidence while fixing
MSP; and
(e) the achievement made by
Government therefrom?
Stopping export of pulses
*93. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that experts have
warned Government to stop export of
pulses because in the year 2005-06 there
has been acute shortage of pulses in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government are now planning to import
the pulses; and
(d) if so, the reasons for importing it
when we had been exporting it earlier?
Wheat quota for Kerala
*94. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the wheat
quota for Kerala for distribution to APL
and BPL card holders has been sharply cut
from June onwards;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether the State Government was
consulted before taking a decision to cut
wheat quota from June onwards;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Shortage of ration wheat
†*95. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any information from different States about
the shortage of wheat for rationing;
(b) if so, the names of the States from
where information has been received about
the shortage of wheat or other cereals
State-wise;
(c) whether Government have
formulated any plan to meet the demand of
wheat for rationing; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
NRHM in Uttar Pradesh
*96. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELF ARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that under
National Rural Health Mission, 65,000
ASHAs were to be selected in the State of
Uttar Pradesh during the year 2005-06;
(b) if so, whether this target has been
achieved and if not, the reasons therefor;
and
(c) what is the status of implementation
of NRHM in Uttar Pradesh?
Monitoring of clinical trials
*97. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some of the
leading pharmaceutical companies have
launched programmes for developing new

30
drugs for curing diseases such as cancer,
diabetes, arthritis, etc.;
(b) if so, the names of companies
together with the products they have
developed/are in the process of developing;
(c) whether the statutory clinical trials
have been completed; if not, the stage at
which these trials are being conducted;
(d) what efforts are being made to avoid
side effects on consumption of such drugs
and whether the developments are
monitored by Government agencies; and
(e) by when these drugs would be ready
for use?
Effect of globalization on agriculture
sector
*98. SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether globalization has adversely
affected our agricultural sector;
(b) if so, what are the remedial measures
that could protect the farming community;
and
(c) the reason for reducing the subsidies
to agriculture sector by Government?
Announcements regarding import of
wheat
*99. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether he had made announce-
ments about import of wheat in February
and March, 2006 when the wheat crop was
still standing on the ground and the
procurement process was starting in
March;
(b) if so, whether Government are aware
that this has created a false sense of
scarcity, which fuelled excess purchase by
private traders and encouraged big farmers
to hoard the wheat produced; and
(c) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Increasing number of AIDS cases
*100. SHRI LALIT SURI:
SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
note of UN AIDS Report on Global AIDS
Epidemic released in May last which states
that estimated AIDS deaths in India during
2005 were over four lakh, which was
highest in the world for the year and also
that India led the HIV/AIDS table with 5-7
million people living with the disease;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto; and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken by
Government to tackle and improve the
situation?

Corporate investment in agriculture
sector
†400. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to encourage corporate investment in
agriculture sector;
(b) if so, the expected positive impact
of the same in agriculture sector; and
(c) whether it would not adversely affect
the marginal farmers alongwith the steps
that would be taken in view of their
interests?
Assistance to Orissa under National
Horticulture Mission
401. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Orissa Government has
requested for Central assistance for
fourteen districts which are not covered by
the National Horticulture Mission;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the time-frame within which it would
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

the matter?
Making farmers self-reliant
402. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
shortage of food in the country is due to
neglect of farmers;
(b) whether Government are also aware
that about 660 million farmers in the country
are not only food producers but consumers
also;
(c) whether there is any policy to
address the problems faced by farmers for
making them self-reliant; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Self-sufficiency in foodgrains
403. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have reviewed
a recent report of the United Nations Food
94

95

inter-alia a ten million tonne decrease in
world wheat production this year with a
strong demand outlook and prices likely to
remain generally high and volatile;

especially in view of the shortage being
faced in our buffer stocks necessitating
massive import of wheat; and
(c) the details of fresh initiatives being
taken to achieve self-sufficiency in
foodgrains and bridge the demand and
supply gap on a durable basis to protect
the interests of the common man?
Modernisation of fisheries sector
404. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
fisheries sector has vast potential in our
country;
(b) if so, the action plan of Government
to modernize this industry with a view to
fully exploit its potential; and

Government to develop this industry in

ICAR agreement with ICRISAT for

(d) if so, the details thereof?

Universities on agricultural research

(a) whether any university or
organisation has entered into an agreement

organisation in the field of agricultural
research;
(b) whether there is any clauses or
section in those agreements which deals
with the patenting rights on the results of
research;
(c) the advantages Government seeks
to get out of these combined research; and
(d) the details of agreement entered
between Acharya NG Ranga University for
Agriculture and its counterpart in US?
Agrarian crisis in Kerala
407. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a Central
Planning Commission team had visited
Kerala to study the spiraling agrarian crisis
in the State driving hundreds of farmers to
suicide;
(b) if so, the details and their findings
and recommendations made; and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken by
the Central Government to solve the
problems being faced by the farmers in the
State?

96

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be

(a) whether the Hon'ble Prime
Minister's visit to Vidarbha explores farmers

(b) if so, the safeguards that the
Ministry proposes to implement; and
(c) whether the WTO conditionalities

farmers to resolve the crisis in the
agriculture?

the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Centre
has announced a special package for the
farmers of certain States;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Orissa is also one of the
beneficiaries; and
(d) if so, the details of the financial and
other support that is proposed to be
rendered to the farmers of this poor and
backward State?
Packages for families of farmers
committed suicides

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Hon'ble Prime
Minister has announced  huge packages to
help the families of the farmers who
committed suicides;
(b) whether these packages and help
would be extended to the other States like
Andhra Pradesh where farmers suicide is a

farmers

KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the existing
agriculture policy has added to the problems
being faced by farmers especially small and
marginal farmers;
(b) whether it is also a fact that despite
the slogan "Second Green Revolution" by
Government, incidents of suicides by
farmers have increased;
(c) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
(d) if not, the details of efforts being

wise; and

accountable for the suicide of farmers?
Production of foodgrains, pulses and
oilseeds

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the productivity of
foodgrains, pulses and oilseeds in our
country is very low in  comparison to China
and other leading countries;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) the details of the steps taken by
Government to provide modern

formulate any package for small farmers to
enhance the agricultural production and to
remove their economic backwardness?

the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have started a scheme called Grameen
Bhandaran Yojana for construction of rural
godowns in the country;
(b) if so, the aims and objectives of the
above scheme;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government
are not going to extent any financial
assistance or otherwise to rural individuals
or corporations, etc.; and

financial assistance to rural individuals or

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:

about the suggestions made by the National

the Minimum Support Price (MSP)
Programme to all crops to provide income
security to small farmers;

also by the NCF like market risk
stabilisation fund jointly by State and
Central Governments, expanding the scope
of agricultural insurance policies, etc.;

acitively the suggestions made by the NCF
to protect the small farmers; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?

profession

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the reasons for farming becoming a
loss making profession particularly for
small/marginal farmers;
(b) the steps taken to make farming a
remunerative profession; and
(c) whether Government would
formulate a scheme to help farmers in
distress to prevent them from falling in debt
trap?
KVK in Goa

NAIK: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
sanctioned a Krishi Vigyan Kendra in  the
South Goa district;
(b) if so, whether the Kendra has started
functioning; and
(c) the details of activities proposed to
be undertaken by the said Kendra?

98

AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:

proposal to purchase more and more cotton

by the CCI during the current year in each
State;
(c) the details of actual production of
cotton in each State; and
(d) how Government are protecting the
interests of cotton farmers?

mangoes

POOJARY: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that harmful
chemicals like calcium carbide are being used
to artificially ripen mangoes;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that no action is
taken by the concerned authorities to
prevent such a practice; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the action
proposed to be taken by Government to
check such hazardous practice?
Setting up of a National Fisheries
Development Board in Hyderabad
419. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a proposal
has been formulated to set up a National
Fisheries Development Board in
Hyderabad to study various aspects of
supporting tuna and deep-sea fishing in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and its
present status; and
(c) the projected estimates of potential
of the tuna and deep-sea fishing in earning
foreign exchange and for employment
generation?
Contract farming

NAIK: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
institutionalize contract farming in the
country;
(b) the names of States, if any, where
the practice is prevalent or is in the pipeline;
(c) whether the concept of contract
farming protects the interest of land holder
farmer; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

Kendras in about 588 rural districts of the
country during the Tenth Five Year Plan;
(b) whether it is also a fact that Indian
Council of Agriculture Research has an
extensive network of  Krishi Vigyan Kendras
under it in about 492 Districts; and
(c) if so, the contribution of Krishi
Vigyan Kendras, so far, in enhancing
knowledge of farmers alongwith increase
in agriculture produce according to set

targets with complete details thereof in the

Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased

(a) the details of incidents of suicide
committed by farmers in Maharashtra,
Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Karnataka and
Tamil Nadu since May, 2004;
(b) the details of official delegations,
including number of visits made, sent by
Government to the regions affected with
incidents of suicides by farmers, State-wise;
(c) the summary of findings and
recommendations made by each delegation
in respect of the regions so visited; and
(d) the net-outcome thereof?
Food security
†423. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that food security
faces serious threat in the country;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
production of foodgrains is on the decline;
and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken by Government in this regard?
Livestock policy
424. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of people engaged
and working in livestock sector;
(b) the contribution of livestock sector
to agriculture and allied activities;
(c) whether Government have
formulated a National Livestock Policy for
the development of this sector; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?

production

BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:

grim farm picture of India, declining

has kept India's food surplus constant at

employment;

Government want equitable development,

considered those suggestions and taken
steps to implement them?

SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken into

100
cognizance the steep rise in the prices of
vegetables in various cities;
(b) if so, the details thereof alongwith
the comparable figures of previous years;
(c) whether it is a fact that the price-
rise has been steeper at retail outlets as
